ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the angle bisectors of $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$ intersect at point $F$. Through point $F$, draw $EG \parallel BC$ intersecting $AB$ and $AC$ at points $E$ and $G$, respectively. If $BE=6$ and $CG=10$, what is the length of segment $EG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $EG\parallel BC$,

it follows that $\angle EFB=\angle FBC$,

since $BF$ bisects $\angle ABC$,

it follows that $\angle EBF=\angle FBC$,

therefore, $\angle EBF=\angle EFB$,

hence $EF=BE$,

similarly, $FG=GC$,

therefore, $EG=EF+FG=BE+GC=\boxed{16}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the attached figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; E is located on side AB, G is located on side AC; segment EG passes through point F, and in the figure is parallel to the base BC, F is located between E and G; segments BF and CF respectively connect from B, C to F. The problem statement says that BF, CF are respectively the angle bisectors of ∠ABC, ∠ACB, and gives BE=6, CG=10. Then reason: because EG ∥ BC, by the angle relationship of parallel lines it can be obtained that ∠EFB = ∠FBC. Also because BF bisects ∠ABC, ∠EBF = ∠FBC. Thus ∠EFB = ∠EBF, triangle EBF is an isosceles triangle, therefore EF = BE = 6. Similarly on the right side, using EG ∥ BC and CF bisecting ∠ACB, it can be obtained that triangle FGC is an isosceles triangle, FG = CG = 10. (More specifically, the parallel lines give ∠GFC = ∠BCF, and the angle bisector gives ∠BCF = ∠FCG, so ∠GFC = ∠FCG, hence FG = CG.) Since E, F, G are collinear and F is between E and G, EG = EF + FG = 6 + 10 = 16.
